links.outcome: AI sensitivity across care settings (inpatient, ED, outpatient) and demographic subgroups within a 17-facility system
links.effect: Overall sensitivity 82.2%; reduced in outpatient setting (72.2%) where subtle hemorrhages were more common; performance consistent across demographic subgroups.
links.quote: Performance was also reduced in the outpatient setting (72.2%), where subtle hemorrhages were more common, while remaining consistent across demographic subgroups.

links.effect: Performance remained consistent across demographic subgroups.

unlisted_practices: Using an LLM (GPT-4o zero-shot with prompt refinement) to extract reference-standard labels from radiology reports for large-scale AI evaluation, validated against 500 manual annotations

screen.reason: Retrospective real-world validation of a commercial diagnostic/triage imaging model (Aidoc ICH) across a large health system cohort, with ground truth established via an LLM annotation pipeline. Tests model diagnostic performance/subgroup performance rather than evaluating an organizational deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
